approach: Frequency map matching across all valid substrings.
observation: For each character ch in S, we know its total count total[ch]. A substring S[start..end] is valid if there exists at least one character ch where count in S[start..end] == total[ch].
bruteForce: Check every pair (start, end), maintain running sub-frequency map, and check if any key's sub-count equals full-count. O(N^2 * 26).
optimalSolution: Compute full frequency map fullFreq. Loop start from 0 to N-1, loop end from start to N-1 while keeping subFreq. On each iteration, if subFreq[ch] == fullFreq[ch], record end - start + 1 and break/continue. Return minimum recorded length.
dryRun: S = 'abcadbcd'. fullFreq: a=2, b=2, c=2, d=2. Substring 'abca' (len 4) has subFreq['a']=2 == fullFreq['a']=2. minLength = 4.
edgeCases: String with unique character appearing once ('xxxy' -> 'xy' has 'y' appearing 1 time)
